en: The *Saptabuddhapitṛmātṛnāman-sūtra*, translated during the Former Wei dynasty (translator lost), was thus heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying in the kingdom of Śrāvastī. In that kingdom there was a woman whose son’s name was...
Because she was called Aṅgulimāla, she was known as the Mother of Aṅgulimāla.
The Buddha, accompanied by five hundred bhikṣus, went to the home of the Mother of Aṅgulimāla and sat upon the palace floor to eat.
After the meal, several dozen bhikṣus gathered in a secluded place and conversed together.

“The Buddha is the supreme deity whom I honor and serve; the Buddha possesses sovereign power over mental transformations—what is there that he cannot do? Having known this, how could one fail to understand the years and lifespans, the parents, the surnames and names, and the number of disciples of the Buddhas of the past and the future?”
"What were the intentions and instructions you implemented?
The Buddha, hearing these matters being discussed by the bhikṣus with his divine ear,
went immediately to where the bhikṣus were and asked them:
"What were you all discussing together just now?

The bhikṣus replied, "We were reflecting that the Buddha’s spiritual power is supreme, his moral virtue is wondrous and profound, and his knowledge is lofty and far-reaching; none can surpass the Buddha."

The Buddha then knows the years of life and lifespan, the parents, the names and clans, the number of disciples, and the practices, aspirations, and instructions of the Buddhas who have already passed away as well as those yet to come.
The Buddha said:
“Excellent! Excellent!”
"It is so. You who practice as śramaṇas should simply keep these various virtues in mind.
Thus spoke the Buddha.
"Do you wish to hear the names and surnames of the Buddhas who have already passed away, as well as those of their parents and disciples?
The bhikṣus replied,
"We wish to hear them."
The Buddha said:
"All listen!
The first Buddha was named Vipaśyin; it has been ninety-one kalpas since he entered parinirvāṇa."
The second Buddha was named Śikhin; thirty-one kalpas have passed since his parinirvāṇa.
The third Buddha was named Viśvabhū; thirty-one kalpas have likewise passed since his parinirvāṇa.
In this Bhadra-kalpa, there shall be two sets of five hundred Buddhas.
The first is Krakucchanda Buddha; the second is Kanakamuni Buddha; the third is Kāśyapa Buddha; and the fourth is I, the Buddha named Śākyamuni.
“Vipaśyin Buddha’s clan was Kauṇḍinya; Śikhin Buddha’s clan was also Kauṇḍinya; Viśvabhū Buddha’s clan was also Kauṇḍinya.
Krakucchanda Buddha’s clan was Kāśyapa; Kanakamuni Buddha’s clan was also Kāśyapa; Kāśyapa Buddha’s clan was also Kāśyapa.”
Now I have become the Buddha Śākyamuni, of the Gautama clan.
Buddha Vipaśyin was of the Kṣatriya caste; Buddha Śikhin was also of the Kṣatriya caste; Buddha Viśvabhū was also of the Kṣatriya caste.
Krakucchanda Buddha was of the Brahmin caste; Kanakamuni Buddha was also of the Brahmin caste; and Kāśyapa Buddha was also of the Brahmin caste.
Now I have become Śākyamuni Buddha of the Kṣatriya caste.
As for Vipaśyin Buddha, his father was named Bandhumat, a Kṣatriya king, and his mother was named Bandhumatī; the kingdom he governed was named Bandhumatī.
The father of Śikhi was named King Ārūṇa-kṣatriya, his mother was named Parā-kṣatriyā, and the kingdom he governed was named Aruṇavatī.
The father of the Buddha Anūpa was King Subhāratī, a kṣatriya; his mother was named Yaśovatī; and the kingdom he governed was called Anūpama.
The father of Krakucchanda Buddha was named Ajita, of the Brahmin caste; his mother was named Śuklā. The country where he resided was named Rāmagrāma, and the king’s name was Sukhiti.
The father of Kanakamuni Buddha was named Yaśasvanta, of the Brahmin caste;
his mother was named Uttara. The country where he resided was named Campeya, and the king’s name was Campa.
As for Kāśyapa Buddha, his father’s name was Ajjita, of the Brahmin caste; his mother’s name was Bandhumatī. The country where he resided was named Vārāṇasī, and its king was named Kiki Vaideha.

Now I have become Śākyamuni Buddha; my father’s name is King Śuddhodana of the Kṣatriya caste, my mother’s name is Mahāmāyā, the kingdom I govern is named Kapilavastu, and the former great king was named Bandhumat.

“Vipaśyin Buddha lived for eighty thousand years; Śikhin Buddha lived for seventy thousand years; Viśvabhū Buddha lived for sixty thousand years; Krakucchanda Buddha lived for forty thousand years; Kanakamuni Buddha lived for thirty thousand years; and Kāśyapa Buddha lived for twenty thousand years.”
Now, as Śākyamuni Buddha, my lifespan is set at one hundred years, whether it be longer or shorter.

The son of Vipaśyin Buddha was named Sudatta Kaṇṭha; the son of Śikhin Buddha was named Atula; the son of Viśvabhū Buddha was named Subhāradatta; the son of Krakucchanda Buddha was named Uttara; the son of Kanakamuni Buddha was named Tīrthikaśreṇya; and the son of Kāśyapa Buddha was named Śātavāha.
Now I am the son of Śākyamuni Buddha, named Rāhula.
When the Buddha Vipaśyin attained the Way and became a Buddha, he was beneath a pāṭala tree.
When Śikhin attained the Way and became a Buddha, he was beneath the Pāṭalī tree.
When Viśvabhū attained the Way and became a Buddha, he was beneath the Sāla tree.
When Krakucchanda Buddha attained the Way and became a Buddha, it was beneath a śirīṣa tree.
When Kanakamuni Buddha attained the Way and became a Buddha, it was beneath an udumbara tree.
When Kāśyapa Buddha attained the Way and became a Buddha, it was beneath a nyagrodha tree.
Now, when I have become Śākyamuni Buddha, it is beneath an āpeta tree.

"The attendant of the Buddha Virocana was named Āluṇ; the attendant of the Buddha Śikhin was named Cāmajja; the attendant of the Buddha Viśvabhū was named Punarvatsa; the attendant of the Buddha Krakucchanda was named Pūti; the attendant of the Buddha Kanakamuni was named Sāti; and the attendant of the Buddha Kāśyapa was named Sabhīmi."
Now that I have become the Buddha Śākyamuni, my attendant is named Ānanda.
The first disciple of Vipaśyin Buddha was named Vaiśya, and his second disciple was named Ghoṣila.
The first disciple of Śikhin Buddha was named Abhiyu, and the second disciple was named Triśaṅku.
The first disciple of Viśvabhū Buddha was named Buddhija, and the second disciple was named Uttara.
The first disciple of Krakucchanda Buddha was named Saṃgīti; the second disciple was named Vellitaka.
The first disciple of Kanakamuni Buddha was named Cakra; the second disciple was named Uttara.
The first disciple of Kāśyapa Buddha was named Jñānakūṭa, and the second disciple was named Pāṭahaka.
Now, as Śākyamuni Buddha, my first disciple is named Śāriputra, and my second disciple is named Maudgalyāyana.

“Vipaśyin Buddha held three assemblies before and after his teaching, during which he preached the sūtras for the bhikṣus. At the first assembly, one hundred thousand bhikṣus all attained arhatship; at the second assembly, ninety thousand bhikṣus all attained arhatship; and at the third assembly, eighty thousand bhikṣus all attained arhatship.”

The Buddha likewise preached the sutras in three assemblies. In the first assembly, he preached the sutras, and ninety thousand bhikṣus all attained arhatship; in the second assembly, he preached the sutras, and eighty thousand bhikṣus all attained arhatship; in the third assembly, he preached the sutras, and seventy thousand bhikṣus all attained arhatship.

The Buddha Suśobhana preached the sūtras on two occasions. At the first assembly, seventy thousand bhikṣus all attained arhatship; at the second assembly, sixty thousand bhikṣus all attained arhatship.
During one assembly when Krakucchanda Buddha preached the sutras, forty thousand bhikṣus all attained arhatship.
During one assembly when Kanakamuni Buddha preached the sutras, thirty thousand bhikṣus all attained arhatship.
In a single assembly when Kāśyapa Buddha preached the sutras, twenty thousand bhikṣus all attained arhatship.
Now, in this single assembly when I, Śākyamuni Buddha, preach the sutras, one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus have all attained arhatship.
The Buddha addressed the bhikṣus, saying:
"The wisdom of a Buddha is immeasurable and beyond all praise; it can know the original parents and the kings under whom the seven Buddhas were born, as well as the deeds those kings performed."
The Buddha told the bhikṣus: "The sūtras must not fail to be studied; the Way must not fail to be practiced.

A Buddha is like a boatman upon the great ocean; tens of millions of people all look up to him to cross the sea. When the Buddha teaches the world, he causes all to do good; that one attains the Way and crosses over the world is likewise so."
Having heard this sutra, the bhikṣus rejoiced, paid their respects, and withdrew.
*The Sutra on the Names of the Parents of the Seven Buddhas*.
